title: Poker Game Value Example
body_html:
Poker Game Value Example

MFoGT Exercise 6.8.2 studies a two-card zero-sum poker game with Nature choosing $H$ or $L$ uniformly and only player 1 observing the card.

After eliminating strictly dominated rows, the relevant normal-form zero-sum game has value $1/3$. Player 1's unique optimal mixed strategy is $$ \frac13(CH,CL)+\frac23(CH,SL). $$ Equivalently, player 1 always continues with a high card and bluffs with a low card with probability $1/3$.

Player 2 checks with probability $2/3$ and stops with probability $1/3$.

References

  • [MFoGT, Exercise 6.8.2 and Hints for Chapter 6, Exercise 2] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MathFoundationsGameTheory.pdf. Zero-sum poker game, normal form, value, and optimal behavioral strategies.
